description.narrative: IISS has submitted a request for core support towards the implementation of its strategy (2021 - 2025) for the next four years. The strategy was developed based on the lessons learned from the previous strategy period (2017 - 2020) and is also informed by the changing peace and security dynamics in the continent. The process of adaptation to the existing COVID-19 context has also been reflected upon in the strategy document. For the strategy period 2021 - 2025, ISS has an overall goal to have evidence-based human security policies and practices is developed and implemented in Africa. The strategy has five outcome areas: - Decision makers on African human security and development challenges are informed by ISS research and analysis - Participants in ISS-convened dialogues & gatherings influence policy debates about human security challenges in Africa - Policies, strategies, programmes in key institutions dealing with Africa’s human security challenges are improved - Stakeholders’ capacity is built to effectively intervene with the aim of improving human security in Africa. - The ISS is an efficient and equitable employer, which develops its staff and encourages collaboration across offices and programmes. The strategy document also presents fourteen thematic topics including: African futures; Gender equality; Africa in the world; Governance, Peace and security; Democratic governance beyond elections; Capacity to prevent, manage and resolve conflicts and sustain peace; Youth peace and security; Maritime security; Migration and forced displacement; Security and governance of new technology; National and trans-national crime and violence; Violent extremism and counter- terrorism; Violence prevention; Criminal justice; and Climate change and human security.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and Institute for Security Studies

description.narrative: During the contribution period, ISS influenced peace and security policy at national, regional and international levels, strengthened institutional capacity, advanced strategic thinking on violent extremism, and enhanced information dissemination through research, networks and digital platforms. Through Sida's core funding, ISS contributed to policy development, analysis, regional cooperation and capacity building across Africa. ISS played a strategic advisory and technical role in shaping peace and security policies and frameworks. It advised Ethiopia's Ministry of Peace on national identity and values in the context of the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement and supported the design of Ethiopia's National Dialogue Process. ISS provided technical guidance to the AU Peace and Security Council, including on sanctions policy, and informed national policies and strategies on preventing violent extremism in countries such as Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso and several Southern African countries. Its support included revisions of counter-terrorism strategies that incorporated non-military approaches and alignment with regional SADC frameworks. ISS also contributed technical expertise that supported South Africa's removal from the FATF grey list and Namibia's progress towards delisting, while acknowledging that these results depended on the efforts of multiple stakeholders. At the continental level, ISS served as the lead technical partner to the African Union in the reform of the African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA). Its recommendations were presented to African leaders in 2025 and informed ongoing discussions on strengthening the AU's peace and security mechanisms. ISS analysis also informed the AU Commission's engagement with the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) and other coup-affected countries, while its methodological and advisory support strengthened AU early warning capacities, particularly in relation to developments in the Great Lakes region. ISS deepened understanding of complex security challenges and promoted more proactive and development-oriented approaches to peace and security. Its research and policy engagement enhanced understanding of violent extremism in the Sahel and contributed to shifting the policy narrative from predominantly military responses towards integrated political, developmental and governance-based strategies. ISS provided analysis and briefings to national governments, regional organisations, the African Union and the United Nations, including contributions to UN Security Council discussions on terror financing, instability in the Sahel and Africa's role in responses to the Islamic State. It delivered more than 70 briefings on political transitions and unconstitutional changes of government in Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso and Guinea, and supported stabilisation planning, evaluation and foresight processes. ISS also strengthened regional cooperation and institutional capacity. It supported initiatives such as the Accra Initiative, the Lake Chad Basin Strategy and SAMIM, provided technical assistance to regional policing bodies, promoted cooperation on transnational organised crime, and advanced maritime security collaboration among West African coastal states. Its recommendations on maritime security were incorporated into the Oceans 20 communiqué, demonstrating uptake in international policy processes. In addition, ISS contributed to the development of regional legislative frameworks and strengthened foresight and scenario-planning capacities in countries such as Malawi and through partnerships with AUDA-NEPAD. Through publications, digital platforms and professional networks, ISS enhanced access to policy-relevant analysis and facilitated information exchange among African policymakers, practitioners and researchers. It produced policy briefings, reports and scenario-planning tools; published ten Peace and Security Council Reports; launched the African Futures website with AI-enhanced functionality; and helped establish the NeTT4Peace network to strengthen collaboration between the AU and African think tanks. Partnerships with AUDA-NEPAD, UNDP and other institutions further supported the integration of foresight and evidence-based analysis into development and security planning across the continent.
